summary: A timeline by Nell Geraets in The Age tracing how Taylor Swift and NFL player Travis Kelce went from a 2016 'Kiss, Marry, Kill' answer to Swift appearing at a Kansas City Chiefs game at Arrowhead Stadium. It follows the failed friendship bracelet at the Eras Tour, podcast hints, media reports of hanging out, and NFL commentators' Swift lyric references. The article stresses nothing confirms a romance but says the pairing has expanded the NFL's audience.
one_line: A timeline of how Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce's rumoured connection grew from a 2016 game answer to Swift attending a Chiefs game in September 2023.
key_facts: In 2016, on AfterBuzz TV, Travis Kelce played 'Kiss, Marry, Kill' with options Taylor Swift, Katy Perry and Ariana Grande, saying he'd kill Grande, marry Perry and kiss Swift.
In July 2023, on the New Heights podcast he shares with his brother, Kelce said he intended to give Swift a friendship bracelet with his number during her Eras Tour concert in Kansas City.
The bracelet never reached Swift; Kelce said she doesn't meet anybody and saves her voice for the 44 songs she sings, so 'I took it personal'.
In August, the Kelce brothers discussed his moustache, which he grows yearly in honour of Chiefs head coach Andy Reid; Kelce said 'something tells me she's going to like it'.
Kelce took a week off training to visit New York City, per Vulture, while Swift was re-recording her 1989 tracks there.
In September it was reported that Swift and Kelce had been 'quietly hanging out' for months, the first media confirmation rather than fan speculation.
On September 17, Kelce scored a touchdown against the Jaguars, and CBS announcer Ian Eagle said 'Kelce finds a blank space for the score', referencing Swift's 2014 hit Blank Space.
NFL Network's Rich Eisen used Swift lyric references like 'shake it off', 'anti-hero' and 'all too well' in a preshow; Kelce commented 'Well played Rich … Well played' on Instagram.
On September 21, Kelce said on The Pat McAfee Show that he had invited Swift to watch one of his games at Arrowhead.
Swift attended the Monday game at Arrowhead Stadium, cheering for No. 87 and appearing to shout 'let's f—ing go' after Kelce's touchdown.
Swift is known as an Eagles fan, being from Pennsylvania and referencing the team in Gold Rush, making her support for the Chiefs notable.
Fans noted Kelce's post-game outfit labelled the '1989 bedroom painting set' and the pair were spotted in a 'getaway car'; Swift re-releases 1989 in October.
The article says none of this confirms Swift and Kelce are dating, but compares the cultural pairing to Kim Kardashian and Kanye West.
